title: 🏭 Back to the Plant — ELEC 2
test_name: ELEC2 Rentrée Diagnostic — Back to the Plant (B1)
story: Max is an apprentice industrial electrician at a food-processing plant near Dijon. Today is his first day back after the summer break, and the workshop smells like coffee and hot metal.
During the summer, the plant never stopped. The night team monitored the production lines, and a contractor replaced the old lighting in warehouse B.
This morning, the supervisor gives Max a work order: "Line 2 stopped twice last week. The operators heard a buzzing noise near the electrical cabinet. Check it before lunch."
Max opens the cabinet and inspects the connections. One wire is loose, and a fuse looks black. "Someone has already opened this door," he thinks — the screws are new.
He tightens the terminal, replaces the fuse, and tests the circuit with his multimeter. The readings are normal now. No short circuit today!

At 11:30, he calls the supplier to order spare parts for the next inspection: two fuses, one relay, and five meters of cable. "Since June, we have changed four fuses on this line," he writes in the report. Line 2 is repaired — welcome back, Max!

industrial electrician.en: a person who installs and repairs electrical systems in factories

monitored.en: watched regularly to check that everything works

buzzing noise.en: a continuous low sound, like a bee

electrical cabinet.en: a metal box that contains electrical equipment and connections

wire.en: a thin metal conductor that carries electricity

loose.en: not firmly fixed — the opposite of tight

fuse.en: a small safety part that breaks the circuit when the current is too high

tightens.en: turns a screw until it is firmly fixed

short circuit.en: a dangerous contact between two points that should not touch

supplier.en: a company that sells parts and materials to your company

spare parts.en: extra components you keep in stock to replace broken ones
